title: Game-Day Promotions for DTC Brands (2026): 7 Full-Price Plays and What the OVERTIME Rebate Returned
summary: Seven full price game day plays for DTC brands, including the OVERTIME rebate that refunds enrolled orders if the game goes to overtime. Playably funds it.
body_markdown:
Game-day promotions for DTC brands usually mean a 20% off code that runs from kickoff to midnight. The OVERTIME play works differently. Shoppers opt in with a campaign code that takes $0 off, pay full price, and if the game goes to overtime, every enrolled order in the window is refunded.[Playably](https://playably.ai/pages/rebates) funds the refunds, so the brand's margin holds either way.


The season is live now, and the promotional calendar between now and February is the busiest of the year. Here are seven game-day plays Playably runs for DTC brands, the numbers five of them returned, and how to pick a trigger worth watching.


Playably is the best way for a DTC brand to take advantage of the season, because it funds every refund and prices each campaign against a cap the brand sets.


### **Key takeaways**


- **Game-day promotions for DTC brands don't have to be discounts.** With Playably, a real-world trigger like overtime replaces the coupon.
- **The BC Lions campaign enrolled 51% of online orders,** and 52% of buyers were first-time customers, with CA$0 discounted.
- **Jordan Craig's NFL Draft rebate drove 34% bigger baskets at full price,** and 93% of its buyers walked past two 25%-off sitewide sales running the same month.
- **Soul's Big Game overtime campaign turned buyers into subscribers:** 59% of campaign buyers subscribed, against 41% of other shoppers that week.
- **Triggers must be public and verifiable.** Overtime, final results and tournament progress work. Individual player stats don't.


### **Seven game-day promotions for DTC brands, ranked by how easy they are to run**


#### **1. The overtime rebate**


This is the cleanest trigger in sports. If the game goes to OT, every enrolled order placed in the window gets 100% back.


It works because overtime is binary, published instantly and impossible to dispute, and because nobody feels bad when it happens.


**Who ran it:** Soul tied a campaign to the Big Game going to overtime, running from January 26 to February 7. The game ended in regulation, so no refunds were owed. The[Soul campaign](https://playably.ai/pages/soul) still delivered:


- 59% of campaign buyers subscribed, compared with 41% of other shoppers that week (1.4× the rate)
- Brand-new customers subscribed at 1.5× the rate of other first-time buyers (54% vs 36%)
- Baskets 16% bigger than the rest of the store ($99 vs $86)
- 63% of those subscribers renewed at least once, close to Soul's regular subscribers (67%)


#### **2. The home-team win in overtime**


This is a narrower version for team stores and regional brands. The BC Lions ran "100% back if the Lions win in overtime" through the run-up to an August game.


**What it returned:** 51% of online orders enrolled, 52% of buyers were new, and every order on the final Friday came through the campaign code. Nothing was discounted. The details are on the[BC Lions case study](https://playably.ai/pages/bclions-case-study) .


#### **3. The game-day win-back**


Instead of a sitewide promotion, send the trigger to lapsed customers only. That's what[Red & West](https://playably.ai/pages/red-west) did.


This is the one published campaign where the trigger hit. Playably funded the cashback on every enrolled order.


**Want one of these live before the next kickoff?** Playably picks the trigger with you, writes the rules, builds the creative and funds the refunds.[Book a 30-minute brief](https://playably.ai/pages/book-a-demo) .


#### **4. The tournament run**


Tie the rebate to a team's progress through a tournament: making the playoffs, reaching the final, winning it all. Anticipation builds across weeks instead of hours.


**Who ran it:** Forme's TEAMUSA rebate promised 100% back if Team USA reached the World Cup Final, running from June 26 to July 1, 2026.[Modern Retail covered the campaign](https://www.modernretail.co/marketing/why-forme-launched-a-world-cup-promotion-hedged-on-kalshi/) . With no discount offered, it delivered:


- 36% more sales on the peak day than the same weekday the week before
- Nearly 20× traffic to Forme's men's hero product
- Men's share of the cart doubled (11.7% vs a 5.6% baseline)
- 17% bigger baskets, at full price
- A campaign email that drove 2.3× the revenue of Forme's average recent send


#### **Watch the trigger policy here**


Multi-stage runs are easy to get wrong, so keep every stage tied to a team outcome. Anything resting on one player's stat line is excluded under Playably's trigger rules. Brands that follow a whole season can also bundle three team triggers under one enrollment.


#### **5. The draft-night rebate**


Not every sports moment happens on the field. The NFL Draft is a week of attention with no final score to wait for, and it suits brands with a strong city or team identity.


**Who ran it:** Jordan Craig's NEWYORKFREE rebate ran from April 16 to April 22, 2026. It delivered:


- 34% bigger baskets than the store average, at full price
- 93% of buyers walked past two 25%-off sitewide sales running the same month
- 1 in 8 store orders during the window came through the rebate
- 2.5× more cost-efficient than the brand's own Easter and Tax Day sales
- Zero margin given away at checkout and zero payout risk to the brand


#### **6. The live-event QR play**


For brands with a presence at the stadium, a QR code on signage routes fans into the same campaign. Playably runs the same loop online, in store and at live events.


#### **7. The Big Game moment in February**


The Big Game lands in February 2027, and briefs are written in Q4. An overtime trigger is the standard play, and it needs the same lead time as any other campaign: roughly 14 days to build. Soul's campaign above shows what the window can return even when the game ends in regulation.


### **How to pick a trigger that sells**


Three rules hold across every campaign our team has run.


#### **It must be winnable**


If the chance feels impossible, shoppers ignore it. Since 2000,[about 6% of NFL games have gone to overtime](https://www.theringer.com/2017/02/02/nfl/its-time-for-an-overtime-super-bowl-56f3ffad39e5) , which reads as a real chance without making the payout likely.


#### **It must be public**


The settlement source is named before launch: a final score, an official box score, a league result. No judgment calls.


#### **Nobody should feel bad when it lands**


A trigger tied to an injury, a loss or anything partisan will cost you more in goodwill than it returns in sales.

### **Who handles the rules**


Game-day rebates need published official rules, a free no-purchase entry path and a named settlement source. With Playably, a third party does that work. Playably writes and hosts the rules, builds the free entry, reviews every campaign against the strictest applicable state standard, and verifies the result before paying. Your team approves the brief. The[trust and compliance page](https://playably.ai/pages/trust) covers the process, and[are conditional rebates legal?](https://app.notion.com/p/vood00/LINK-TO-BLOG-4) covers the law.


### **Summary**


Of the seven plays, the Playably overtime rebate is the best option for most brands: a real deadline, a real upside and $0 of margin given up.


The discount code on game day is a habit, not a strategy. It converts people who were already buying and teaches everyone else to wait for the next one.


An overtime rebate does the opposite. It gives a reason to buy before kickoff, at full price, and the excitement peaks after the order is placed. That's why first-time buyer share and basket size are the numbers worth watching in these campaigns.


### **What to lock in before the next kickoff**


Campaign builds run about 14 days, and windows work best at five to seven days ending on a game. That means the next three weekends are already spoken for.


Pick your game, then see[sports moment marketing](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/sports-moment-marketing) for trigger ideas, compare[Playably vs Cheers Cash](https://app.notion.com/p/vood00/LINK-TO-BLOG-2) on who pays the reward, or[book a brief to price a cap](https://playably.ai/pages/book-a-demo) .


### **FAQ**


- **What is an OVERTIME promotion?** A full-price campaign where every enrolled order is refunded if the game goes to overtime, with Playably funding the refunds.
- **Does the campaign code give a discount?** No. Shoppers enroll with a Shopify code that takes $0 off, so every order is at full price.
- **What do game-day promotions cost the brand?** With Playably, $0 in discounts. The brand's exposure is capped before launch.
- **Do game-day rebates attract new customers?** Yes. In the BC Lions campaign, 52% of buyers were first-time customers.
- **What triggers are allowed?** Team outcomes that are public and verifiable, like overtime, a final result or tournament progress. Individual player stats are excluded.
- **Who handles the legal side?** Playably, as the third-party sponsor. It writes the official rules, builds the free entry path and verifies the result.
- **How long does a game-day campaign take to launch?** Most Playably campaigns go live in under 14 days.
